title: Give the agent a way to check its own work
body: Agents get much better when they can run something that says pass or fail: a test suite, a linter, a build command. Put the exact command in your prompt ("run npm test until it passes") and the agent can fix its own mistakes before you ever see them.

title: Keep a project instructions file
body: Most coding agents read a project file such as CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md on every run. Put your stack, conventions, commands and "never do X" rules there once instead of repeating them in every prompt.

title: Ask for a plan before edits
body: For anything bigger than a one-line fix, ask the agent to outline its plan first and approve it. It's the cheapest moment to catch a wrong approach, before tokens are spent on code you'll throw away.

title: Small tasks beat big ones
body: One well-scoped task ("fix the logout bug, here's how to reproduce it") succeeds far more often than "improve the auth system". Split big goals into steps you can verify one at a time.

title: Paste the real error
body: Give the agent the full error message, stack trace or failing output rather than a summary. The exact text is usually the fastest route to the cause.

title: Commit before you let an agent loose
body: Start every agent session from a clean git state. If the run goes sideways, one command gets you back, and the diff shows exactly what the agent changed.

title: Use cheaper models for cheaper work
body: Bring-your-own-key agents let you pick the model. Use a fast, cheap model for boilerplate, renames and docs, and save the expensive model for debugging and design decisions.

title: Measure cost per solved task, not per run
body: An agent that costs twice as much per run but solves the task first time is cheaper than one that needs three attempts. Track what you spend per working result.

title: Multi-agent setups need a referee
body: When several agents work together, give one of them (or a test) the job of checking the others' output. Without a verification step, agents happily agree on wrong answers.

title: Describe the outcome, not the steps
body: For writing, design and marketing agents, say who it's for, what it should achieve and what good looks like, then show one example. You'll get better work than with a step-by-step recipe.
